title: Increase Premium transfer limit from $50 000 to $100 000
requestSummary: Raise the daily outbound wire-transfer ceiling for customers on the Premium tier from the current hard-coded cap of $50 000 to $100 000. The change must propagate consistently across the core-banking validation service, the mobile-banking API gateway, the customer-facing React Native app (display and input guard), and the compliance audit-log schema. Regulatory guidance (BSA / AML Pillar 3) requires that any threshold change is accompanied by an enhanced-due-diligence flag when the new limit is first exercised.
openQuestions: Should the $100 000 limit also apply to batch (scheduled) transfers, or only to manual single transfers initiated in-app?
Is the Premium tier defined by a contract flag in the CRM, or by a computed balance/product rule in core-banking? Both codepaths exist; confirm which is authoritative.

The compliance team's wire-transfer review queue triggers at ≥ $10 000 (FINCEN threshold). The existing 'large-transfer' alert fires at $50 000. Does the alert threshold change too, or stay at $50 000?
Four mobile-app localisation strings hard-code '$50,000'. Are these surfaced to end users in a visible error message, or only in internal logs?

The fraud-scoring model has a feature 'transfer_amount_vs_tier_limit_ratio'. Raising the limit will change the distribution of that feature for Premium customers — has the model been retrained or validated?

entryPoints.label: POST /internal/transfers/validate
entryPoints.description: Core-banking internal REST endpoint that performs limit enforcement, AML checks, and account-balance verification before authorising a transfer. All downstream systems must call this before crediting.

entryPoints.label: POST /api/v2/transfers
entryPoints.description: Public-facing API Gateway endpoint consumed by the mobile app and third-party integrators. Delegates limit checks to the core service but also enforces a gateway-level rate limit and tier validation.

entryPoints.label: TransferScreen — React Native
entryPoints.description: Mobile entry point where users compose and submit a transfer. Contains client-side validation that rejects inputs above the displayed limit before making a network call.

items.label: Premium daily outbound transfer ceiling
items.description: Hard-coded constant PREMIUM_DAILY_LIMIT = 50000 used as the authoritative cap inside the core-banking limit-policy engine. Changing this constant is the primary mechanical change required by the ticket.

evidence.snippet: if (tier === 'premium' && amount > PREMIUM_DAILY_LIMIT) throw new LimitExceededError(PREMIUM_DAILY_LIMIT);

items.label: Standard daily outbound transfer ceiling
items.description: Standard-tier limit is $10 000. Not changed by this ticket but defined in the same file — confirm no accidental edits.

items.label: Large-transfer compliance alert threshold
items.description: Fires a compliance event when transfer ≥ $50 000. Currently coincides with the Premium limit, so all limit-ceiling transfers trigger an alert. After the change, transfers between $50 000 and $100 000 will NOT trigger this alert unless the threshold is also updated — likely a compliance gap.

issues.description: After raising PREMIUM_DAILY_LIMIT to $100 000, transfers between $50 000–$100 000 by Premium customers will bypass the LARGE_TRANSFER_THRESHOLD alert. This contradicts the stated BSA/AML obligation. Confirm whether LARGE_TRANSFER_THRESHOLD should also increase or remain at $50 000.

items.label: API Gateway tier-limit config
items.description: The gateway duplicates the limit in its own config file as a guard before proxying to core. Must be updated in sync, otherwise the gateway will reject valid Premium transfers before they reach core-banking.

evidence.snippet: export const TIER_LIMITS: Record<string, number> = { standard: 10_000, premium: 50_000, private: 250_000 };

items.label: Mobile app TRANSFER_LIMITS constant
items.description: Client-side constant in the React Native app used for input validation and UI display. If not updated, users will see a false 'limit exceeded' error for amounts between $50 000–$100 000 despite the server accepting them.

evidence.snippet: export const TRANSFER_LIMITS: Record<string, number> = { standard: 10_000, premium: 50_000 };

items.label: Mobile i18n string with hard-coded '$50,000'
items.description: English localisation file contains a user-visible error message with the literal '$50,000'. This will display the wrong limit after the change.

evidence.snippet: "transfer.limitExceeded": "Amount exceeds your daily limit of $50,000 for Premium accounts."

items.label: Compliance audit log schema — limit_at_time field
items.description: The audit schema snapshots the effective limit at the time of each transfer. If the schema has a CHECK constraint or enum that validates the stored value, it will reject the new $100 000 value. A schema migration is required.

items.label: Gateway → Core: POST /internal/transfers/validate
items.description: The API Gateway proxies every transfer initiation to the core-banking validate endpoint. Both sides must agree on the limit semantics. If core raises its limit but the gateway does not, the gateway will block valid requests.

evidence.snippet: const res = await fetch(`${CORE_BASE_URL}/internal/transfers/validate`, { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify(payload) });

items.label: Mobile → Gateway: POST /api/v2/transfers
items.description: The React Native app calls the public gateway endpoint to initiate transfers. Client-side limit validation mirrors the server-side cap, so both must be updated together.

items.label: Core: limitPolicy unit tests
items.description: Existing test suite covers the $50 000 boundary. Must be updated to cover $100 000 boundary and intermediate values.

items.label: Gateway: tierGuard middleware tests
items.description: Tier guard test asserts 422 for amount > 50000 on premium tier. Will break after the config change and must be updated.

effortEstimate: 9 files to change across 3 repositories, ~80 lines net. Schema migration required. Estimated 2–3 engineer-days including regression testing.
riskRationale: Rated HIGH: (1) the change crosses three production repositories with independent deployment pipelines; (2) a compliance audit-schema migration is required, which carries database rollback risk; (3) the fraud-scoring ML model has a ratio feature keyed to the old limit, potentially degrading model accuracy until retrained; (4) four i18n strings in three languages display the old limit; (5) the large-transfer compliance alert gap ($50k–$100k) is a potential regulatory exposure if not resolved before deployment.

changePlan.action: Update PREMIUM_DAILY_LIMIT in core-banking limit policy
changePlan.rationale: This is the authoritative source of the limit. All other changes must be consistent with this value.

changePlan.action: Add 100_000 to the auditSchema Zod union and write a DB migration script
changePlan.rationale: The compliance audit log has a CHECK constraint on limit_at_time. Without this migration, every new-limit transfer will fail the schema validation and be rejected at audit-log write time.

changePlan.action: Decide and document the large-transfer alert threshold stance with Compliance
changePlan.rationale: The LARGE_TRANSFER_THRESHOLD at $50 000 creates a regulatory gap for $50k–$100k Premium transfers. Either raise the threshold (requires Compliance sign-off) or add a separate Premium-tier alert rule. Do not proceed to production without written confirmation.

changePlan.action: Update TIER_LIMITS in the API Gateway config and redeploy the gateway
changePlan.rationale: The gateway independently enforces limits. If not updated, it will reject valid Premium transfers before they reach core-banking, causing customer-visible 422 errors.

changePlan.action: Update TRANSFER_LIMITS constant and i18n strings in the mobile app
changePlan.rationale: Client-side validation mirrors the server cap. Stale constants produce false 'limit exceeded' UI errors. Localisation strings in en.json, fr.json, es.json, de.json contain the literal '$50,000' and must be updated.

changePlan.action: Update and extend unit tests across all three repositories
changePlan.rationale: Existing tests assert the $50 000 boundary and will fail after the config change. New tests must cover the $100 000 boundary, intermediate values, and the unchanged standard-tier limit.

changePlan.action: Co-ordinate with the Data Science team to retrain or validate the fraud-scoring model
changePlan.rationale: The 'transfer_amount_vs_tier_limit_ratio' feature distribution shifts for Premium customers. Deploying without retraining may silently degrade fraud detection accuracy until the next scheduled model refresh.

changePlan.action: Deploy in order: core-banking → API Gateway → mobile app (staged rollout)
changePlan.rationale: Deploying core first ensures the backend is ready before the gateway starts routing the new limit. Mobile app must be deployed last; a brief window where core and gateway accept the new limit but the mobile app still blocks it client-side is acceptable and safe.
